camping.summary: Camping is generally allowed under everyman's-right style wilderness guidance, but area exceptions such as Ánnjaloanji Protected Area can prohibit camping/fire.
Tenting is allowed in the hut yard, but field reports repeatedly describe the hut surroundings as rocky and tent spots as limited.

fire.summary: General guidance allows fires without separate permission in some contexts, but scarce-wood fell terrain means fires are discouraged and wildfire warnings must be checked.
Do not model an outdoor fireplace unless an official fire site is separately verified. Hut firewood is for hut heating; outdoor campfires are forbidden where no official fire site exists.

Public lean-to and dry toilet are confirmed by Luontoon API, but a separate firewood/fireplace record remains ambiguous because the nearby yrityskota is private/rental and the public lean-to does not expose a separate official fireplace coordinate.

season.summary: Summer hiking route. Recommended hiking window is roughly early July to early September or mid-September depending source wording. Saarijärvi is not accessible during thaw/break-up conditions; ski-touring season is March-April.

dogs.summary: Dogs/pets must be leashed in Käsivarsi. Saarijärvi Kiiruna reservable hut prohibits pets. If a route alignment briefly enters Norway, border-crossing pet rules require separate advance checks.

reindeer.summary: Käsivarsi is a special reindeer-herding area; avoid disturbing reindeer and close reindeer-fence gates.

hunting.summary: Eräluvat lists Käsivarsi as small-game hunting area 1613. Hikers may encounter legal seasonal hunting activity.

phoneAndEmergency.summary: Call 112 in emergencies. Mobile dead zones exist; official advice is to check operator coverage, move to higher/open ground, expect possible Norwegian roaming near the border, keep phone warm and bring backup power.

notes: No official stage-1 closure was found in the section pass.

Eräluvat Saarijärvi Kiiruna current notices found by rules lane were administrative/booking related: 2026-04-22 2027 booking opening, 2026-04-13 customer-service closure dates, 2026-03-24 updated booking terms.

Luontoon notice dated 2025-06-24 says the former south-side Saana summer route through the protected grove area was removed from summer use and Kalottireitti is routed north of Saana; this is a geometry-currentness blocker for old GPX/OSM lines near Kilpisjärvi/Saana.

Luontoon conditions notice dated 2025-06-27 reported snow on Kilpisjärvi-Halti / Kalottireitti, difficult foot travel, and potentially challenging water crossings. Treat as seasonal safety evidence, not a current closure.

Luontoon notice dated 2026-02-09 says the Kilpisjärvi-Halti spring-winter maintenance track was marked with twigs via Kalottireitti huts but is not maintained for skiers and has no condition guarantee. Do not reuse it as summer navigation geometry.

Luontoon avalanche notice dated 2026-03-07 reported avalanches observed at Saana and Malla and avalanche risk 3/5 widely in northern Lapland fells. Add winter/spring avalanche hazard context; not a summer-stage closure.
Metsähallitus stomach-flu/norovirus advisory dated 2025-01-08 affected Saarijärvi and nearby huts/toilets; resolved update dated 2025-07-09 reported Kalottireitti open for normal hiking again.
The active Luontoon route page/API carried a 2026 under-construction route-page/source-currentness signal during this pass. Re-check the official route page before final normalization.

conditionReports.summary: Started near Kilpisjärvi Visitor Centre and reported the first day to Saarijärvi as just over 12 km. Tented in the Saarijärvi hut yard. Confirms the old Saarijärvi hut was closed and the 2023 open/reservable huts were in use.

Return day Saarijärvi-Kilpisjärvi listed as 12 km. Route was rocky/wet but relatively straightforward, briefly entered Norway, reached Tsahkaljärvi before a final gravel-road descent to Kilpisjärvi Visitor Centre. Endpoint evidence: old Saarijärvi hut was closed and the new hut was a couple hundred meters back.

Used train to Rovaniemi and bus to Kilpisjärvi. Saarijärvi-Kilpisjärvi was windy/rainy with boulder fields, wet marshes, fatigue and a long-feeling Norway passage. Supports demanding-weather framing rather than geometry decisions.

Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi reported as 18 km when including access/logistics from camping/supermarket; hut table gives Kilpis camping/hotel to Saarijärvi as 11.8 km. Trail fairly easy to follow, slight climb to Tsahkaljärvi, many day hikers early then quieter; strong wind at Saarijärvi and author slept inside hut.
conditionReports.confidence: high for field conditions, medium for section distance because of access inclusion

conditionReports.summary: Low wooden posts with orange tips can disappear behind rocks. Early terrain rocky and challenging despite moderate ascent. Dry conditions made water levels low; normal water levels likely mean wetter, muddier and more slippery travel. Intermittent mobile coverage at Saarijärvi.

Stage listed as 12 km. First kilometer from nature centre to Tsahkaljärvi was easy, then terrain became progressively rockier with wet patches. Good tent spot found about 0.5 km before huts; hut surroundings very rocky.
Full Kilpisjärvi-Halti reviews note poles are useful for rocky terrain and crossings, route condition was reported great in late summer 2023, huts/toilets clean and used. Not stage-specific.

Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi reported as 13 km and 3:25. Start on gravel walking route, path clear/easy to follow, then winding through rocks and small mounds. Saarijärvi hut visible long before arrival; tent spots limited due rocky/uneven ground, with better spots across a bridge.

Older but detailed report: route from Tsahkaljärvi ascends moderately by a reindeer fence and briefly enters Norway. Saarijärvi not ideal for tenting because of rocks; water taken from streams/rivers as personal practice.

sourceContradictions.details: Reisa and the previous Luontoon itinerary evidence list Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi as 11 km. Current Luontoon API exposes the whole Kalottireitti 76.65 km route but not a Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi section row. Metsähallitus/Eräluvat/current hut context often says Saarijärvi huts are about 12 km from Kilpisjärvi Visitor Centre. OSM relation measures about 12.8 km raw and E1 GPX measures 18.4 km because it follows a broader access/E1 alignment.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use 11 km as the official listed section distance with a source-qualified caveat. Compute app geometry distance only after clipping/reversing the chosen line and resolving the hut-yard endpoint/spur.

sourceContradictions.details: Metsähallitus/Luontoon announced on 2025-06-24 that the former south-side Saana summer route was removed from summer use and Kalottireitti routed north of Saana. The current Luontoon API/OGC route source is official, but any older GPX/OSM line near Saana/Kilpisjärvi may be stale.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Cross-check and preferably clip the current Luontoon/Metsähallitus OGC line before publication.

sourceContradictions.details: OSM/E1 route endpoint aligns with an older Saarijärvi hut/bridge cluster around 69.0624582, 21.0917517, while official 2023/current hut-yard coordinates sit about 300 m away. Field reports in 2024-2025 explicitly describe the old hut as closed and the new hut as the current overnight destination.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Use the current hut yard as app endpoint/facility destination, suppress old hut as a facility, and keep the old cluster only as a route-line endpoint/gap note if using OSM geometry.

sourceContradictions.details: Luontoon confirms the public lean-to and dry toilet, while Kilpisjärven Ladut/OSM/Luontoon unpublished amenity evidence indicates a nearby yrityskota/vuokrakota is private/rental.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Import the public lean-to and dry toilet. Suppress the rental/private kota as a normal public facility.

sourceContradictions.details: General Käsivarsi guidance is more permissive about fires and mentions waste containers in broad terms. Saarijärvi hut-specific guidance is stricter about outdoor fire/no official fire site and firewood for hut heating. Luontoon/Retkikartta exposes a new Saarijärvi waste-storage structure, but Eräluvat/hut guidance can still say visitors must pack out waste or that no waste management is provided.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Prefer hut-specific fire rules. If importing Saarijärvi waste/recycling, include a pack-out caveat and do not present it as guaranteed general waste disposal.

sourceContradictions.details: Malla Strict Nature Reserve rules are stricter than Käsivarsi rules but apply only if modeling the Malla/Three-Country Cairn alternate or connector, not the main Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi stage by default.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Avoid over-applying Malla restrictions to this section.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: Section packet is complete enough for handoff/review. It is not ready for automated import because geometry endpoint decisions and several facility coordinates need one later targeted normalization pass.

Targeted pass improved section 1 substantially: official Luontoon OGC Features route-line evidence is now recorded, OSM reverse/trim metrics are independently confirmed, current Saarijärvi hut-yard facilities are high-confidence, Tsahkaljärvi public facilities are resolved, and new 2024-2025 field/currentness reports are added. Keep not automated-import-ready because a section-specific clipped/exported geometry and Saarijärvi hut-yard spur/endpoint model still need normalization.

openQuestions: During normalization, should the route geometry terminate at the current Saarijärvi open hut point, at a hut-yard centroid, or at the old route-line endpoint plus an explicit spur/gap to the current hut yard?
Clip and export the Luontoon/Metsähallitus OGC MultiLineString for the exact Kilpisjärvi-Saarijärvi section, then compare it against OSM relation 9518275 after the 2025 Saana reroute.
Decide whether confirmed bridge records should become app detail facilities or remain descriptive geometry/safety notes.
Decide whether Saarijärvi wood shed and waste/recycling should be separate import rows or folded into hut details with pack-out and hut-heating-only caveats.
Confirm 2026 summer Arctic Route/Eskelinen/Matkahuolto schedules before publishing public transit guidance.

blockers: Section-specific route geometry still needs clipping/export from Luontoon OGC data or reverse/trim from OSM.
Saarijärvi current hut-yard endpoint/spur must be reconciled with old route-line endpoint before navigation-grade import.

If continuing Phase 2 research, proceed to section 2 (Saarijärvi-Kuonjarjohka) with the required six-agent process; if normalizing section 1 first, clip/export Luontoon OGC linework and model the Saarijärvi hut-yard endpoint/spur.
